Write to me a script about: Title: Artificial intelligence and its evolution through generations

introduction:
In a rapidly changing technological landscape, the convergence of artificial intelligence and industry has given rise to a revolutionary field known as artificial intelligence. This video delves into the fascinating history of artificial intelligence, examining its origins and the milestones that have shaped its evolution over time.

The first generation: manual processes and the advent of automation:
The first generation of artificial intelligence saw industries relying heavily on manual processes. However, the need for efficiency and productivity led to the introduction of basic automation systems such as conveyor belts and assembly lines. This era laid the foundation for artificial intelligence, recognizing the ability of machines to perform repetitive tasks but with limited decision-making capabilities.

The second generation: digitization and data collection:
The second generation brought about a massive change with the advent of computers and the digitization of industrial processes. This era was characterized by the collection and preservation of large amounts of data, which enabled better monitoring and monitoring of industrial processes. SCADA systems enabled real-time data collection, process optimization, and decision-making, but intelligence was rule-based and lacked advanced analytical capabilities.

The third generation: machine learning and advanced analytics:
With the exponential increase in computing power and the availability of large amounts of data, industries have begun to use machine learning algorithms to extract information from complex data sets. Predictive maintenance, quality control and optimization processes are beginning to improve efficiency and reduce costs.

The fourth generation: artificial intelligence and cognitive systems:
The current era of artificial intelligence is characterized by the integration of artificial intelligence and cognitive systems. Technologies such as deep learning and natural language processing enable machines to simulate human intelligence and make decisions. Industrial systems with cognitive capabilities can recognize patterns, process unstructured data, and participate in human-machine collaboration, paving the way for autonomous robots, smart factories, and adaptive manufacturing systems.

future prospects:
Looking ahead, the future of AI looks very bright, with continued advances in robotics, Internet of Things (IoT), and edge computing. 5G technology is expected to enable seamless communication, real-time decision making, and the integration of physical and digital systems into an integrated ecosystem. AI will enable hyper-personalization, dynamic supply chains, and sustainable manufacturing practices, ushering in an era of unprecedented productivity and innovation.

Conclusion:
Artificial intelligence has come a long way since its inception, evolving over multiple generations. From manual processes to the integration of AI and cognitive systems, every step has improved industrial processes, efficiency and decision-making. The potential of AI to transform industries and revolutionize the way we work is limitless. Through continuous progress and concerted efforts, the next generation of artificial intelligence holds the key to opening new horizons for productivity and sustainable growth.

from shapely.geometry import Polygon, Point
from itertools import groupby
import datetime

INF_TIME = 100000000000


class Grid:
    def __init__(self, width, height, obstacles=None):
        self.grid = None
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.obstacles = obstacles
        self.create_grid()

    def create_grid(self):
        self.grid = np.zeros((self.height, self.width), dtype=np.int8)
        for obstacle in self.obstacles:
            polygon = Polygon(obstacle)
            x, y = np.meshgrid(np.arange(self.width), np.arange(self.height))
            points = np.vstack((x.flatten(), y.flatten())).T
            points_inside = np.array([polygon.contains(Point(point)) or polygon.boundary.contains(Point(point)) for point in points])
            self.grid[points_inside.reshape(self.height, self.width)] = 1
        return

    def has_obstacles(self):
        return self.obstacles is not None

    def plot(self):
        plt.imshow(self.grid, cmap='gray')
        plt.show()


class GridGenerator:

        self.objects = objects
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.grids = []
        self.generate_grids()

    def is_inside(self, x, y):
        return 0 <= x < self.width and 0 <= y < self.height and all(g[2].grid[y, x] != 1 for g in self.grids)

        raise ValueError(f"No grid found for time {time}")

            polygons = []

            # Add new objects to current_objects as long as their start time is within the current time range

prompt:
Write a covering letter for the post of Manager - Event Operations based on below details, addressing to the Recruitment Manager at Rugby Canada:

Event Planning and Delivery:
•	Build effective relationships with all stakeholders involved in designated events in cities allocated to the role – match venues, funding partners, hotel partners, local city authorities, contractors, commercial partners and suppliers.
•	Drive collaboration and alignment with internal Rugby Canada and external (e.g. World Rugby) Functional Areas - Competitions, Ticketing, Commercial, MarComms, Merchandise, Broadcast and Development.
•	Responsible and accountable for relevant event budget line items.
Venue Operations:
•	Lead the planning and delivery for all match venue operations and act as the main point of contact for all event functional areas (e.g. broadcast, officials, teams, media etc).
•	Lead relationship with match venue representatives to determine space allocation, staffing and security, FF&E, power, and IT requirements.
•	Work with Director, Events in the negotiation and execution of match venue contracts in association with the event calendar. 
•	Develop and execute event operational plans including project plans, stadium maps, production schedules, staff resourcing/scheduling, signage plans, back of house F&B, space allocation and requirements. 
•	Develop and own efficient relationships with all external suppliers and service providers as it relates to the match venue. 
•	Support event experiential delivery such as game presentation programming and activations. 
•	Recruit, train and manage contractors, as required, to support operational deliverables for each event. 
•	Manage the delivery of event volunteer programs, including leadership over contractors as needed. 
•	Lead the development and delivery for event accreditation including zoning, pass design, management, and distribution, including leadership over contractors as needed. 
•	Support the Director, Events in the creation and maintaining of RFPs and MOUs with host cities/venues, local organizing groups and Provincial Unions for events and domestic competitions. 
•	Work with Director, Events on collecting post event surveys and reports to capture valuable feedback on how to improve venue operations for future events. 
Match Management and Competition: 
•	Work with Rugby Canada’s Chief Medical Officer to develop the medical services plan for events in accordance with World Rugby and Rugby Canada guidelines and standards. 
•	Work with Rugby Canada Match Official (MO) Manager to coordinate the Match Official, Citing and Disciplinary team logistics for events including their allocation, flights, accommodation, meals, training venues, ground transport, event day communications and technical requirements. 
•	Work collaboratively with anti-doping authorities / World Rugby representatives to coordinate in stadium requirements for the anti-doping team. 
•	Support the Director, Events in the creation of tournament schedules and match run sheets. 
General: 
•	Ability to serve as lead Event Manager for select Rugby Canada events. 
•	Support the logistics for event staff including flights, accommodation, ground transport and meals/per diems. 
•	Maintain and manage event equipment, managing the storage, shipping and inventory of all event equipment as needed. 

My QUALIFICATIONS
•	8+ years’ event operations experience in the sport or event industry 
•	15+ years’ overall career experience including marketing and event management and activations.
•	MBA from Australian Institute of Business (AIB) and a professional marketing qualification from Chartered Institute of Marketing, UK (CIM UK)
My EXPERIENCE
•	I have experience managing team sponsorships, tournament sponsorships, sports marketing initiatives and campaign and event operations for all national sports in Sri Lanka including, Sri Lanka Cricket, Rugby, Netball, Volleyball, Football, National Paralympics, Army Paralympics, Domestic Cricket big matches, Schools Rugby League and Knockout tournaments.
•	I have experience in dealing with all stakeholders including media, and other sponsors when executing sports events
•	I have experience in sponsorship asset management including sports marketing, developing and promoting sports merchandise and generating revenue
•	I have experience in major international events management, specifically in the planning and delivery of complex events involving multiple stakeholders, requiring integrated planning and execution – across multiple client groups including elite sporting teams and officials, international broadcasters, media, spectators, guests. 
•	I have demonstrable success in planning and delivering at venue and event level – preferably with multiple activations occurring on the same site. 
•	I have experience in a fast-paced environment and capable of moving seamlessly between strategic, tactical, and operational levels of activity. 
•	I have experience dealing with budgets and project management.

On Thursday, Zoom Video Communications announced that it had fired Greg Tomb, the company's president, effective immediately. Tomb had only joined the company in June and was responsible for overseeing Zoom's go-to-market strategy, revenue efforts, and the office of the Global CIO.

The termination of Tomb's employment was without cause, according to a regulatory filing by the company. Tomb will receive severance benefits in accordance with his arrangements. Zoom has not announced whether they will appoint a new president to replace Tomb.

Sterling Auty, an analyst at SVB MoffettNathanson, noted that Tomb's firing came after Zoom's latest outlook implied "a bigger deceleration than the Street had modeled" for enterprise growth. Auty also added that sales leadership transitions typically take three quarters to play out.

Zoom's CEO, Eric Yuan, announced layoffs in early February that impacted 15% of staff and included pay cuts for executives. This move was likely due to the company's softening demand.

Tomb had taken a high-profile role at Zoom during his short tenure, appearing on earnings calls and overseeing the company's sales operation. He reported directly to CEO Eric Yuan, who founded Zoom in 2011 and rapidly built up the business during a pandemic-fueled boom. However, with more competition entering the market and Zoom's growth rate slowing down, Tomb's departure may be seen as a strategic move to restructure the company.

Tomb's employment package included a $45 million stock grant that would vest over four years, in addition to a $400,000 base salary with an 8% bonus target, according to a June filing.

In an interview with Bloomberg during the January World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, Tomb spoke optimistically about Zoom's growth potential while acknowledging that the company faced more competition. Just a few weeks later, Zoom announced its plan to cut 15% of its workforce.

The news of Tomb's departure has affected Zoom's shares, which were down 0.9% in after-hours trading on Thursday. The company's stock has lost 42% over the past 12 months, while the S&P 500 has declined by 9%.

In conclusion, the departure of Zoom's president, Greg Tomb, highlights the company's ongoing efforts to restructure and adapt to the changing landscape of the videoconferencing market. While the move may be a setback for Zoom in the short term, it could ultimately position the company for future success.

prompt:
Create a perfect headline title about these articles TikTok is setting a 60-minute daily screen time limit for users who are aged under 18.

If young people hit the new limit, they will have to enter a passcode to continue to use the service that day.

But they will be able to opt out of the new measure, which TikTok says will be rolled out "in the coming weeks".

The video app, which is owned by Chinese firm ByteDance, said it is introducing the feature to help people "stay in control" of their use.

TikTok said the new limit comes after it brought in a prompt last year to encourage teens to manage their screen time. It said this helped "increase the use of our screen time tools by 234%".

Users of the platform have to be at least 13, and, as part of this new feature, anyone under the age of 18 will receive a weekly notification with a "recap of their screen time".

No 'right amount' of screen time
Users affected will receive their new time limit passcode on a screen in their app as the changes take effect.

Anyone who opts out of the new 60-minute restriction, but goes on to use the app for 100 minutes a day, will receive a prompt from TikTok to set their own screen time controls.

Parents of children using the Family Pairing option on the app will also be able to set screen time limits, as well as access a dashboard which would give a breakdown of app usage.

Cormac Keenan, head of trust and safety at TikTok, said the company had worked with researchers in developing the new limits.

"While there's no collectively endorsed position on the 'right' amount of screen time, or even the impact of screen time more broadly, we consulted the current academic research and experts from the Digital Wellness Lab at Boston Children's Hospital in choosing this limit," he said.

Critics of the video app welcomed the screen time limit, but described it as the "tip of the iceberg" when it comes to TikTok's response to young users' exposure to the platform.

'Crack cocaine of algorithms'
Imran Ahmed is a chief executive of the Center for Countering Digital Hate, which recently published research showing TikTok's algorithm "bombards" teenagers with harmful content.

"TikTok has won the race for the hearts and minds of 14 to 24-year-olds in the United States and the United Kingdom," he said.

"It is the crack cocaine of algorithms. It is the most addictive, it is the most dangerous and the one that needs to be dealt with most urgently."

Mr Ahmed told the BBC his centre's research at the end of last year found that within minutes of opening a TikTok account, a 13-year-old girl user was receiving eating disorder and self-harm content in her feed.

He called on the platform to focus its efforts not just on curbing screen time, but also to "clean up" feeds of harmful content to make it a "safe environment for children".

It comes as TikTok faces renewed controversy over its relationship with the Chinese government and protection of user data.

Earlier this week, the Canadian government became the latest to ban the app from government devices, following similar moves in the United States.

In September 2021, TikTok said it had hit more than one billion active monthly users, making it one of the biggest social sites in the world.

It does not release a demographic breakdown of its users, but is viewed by social media marketers and advertisers as being a key platform to reach people under the age of 34.

TikTok has announced a batch of new features intended to reduce screen time and improve the well-being of its younger users.

In the coming weeks, a daily screen time limit of 60 minutes will be automatically applied to every TikTok user under 18 years old. Teens that hit this limit will be asked to enter a passcode to continue watching. They can disable the feature entirely, but if they do so and spend more than 100 minutes on TikTok a day, they’ll be prompted to set a new limit.

TikTok claims these prompts increased the use of its screen time management tools by 234 percent during the feature’s first month of testing. Teens will also be sent an inbox notification each week that recaps their screen time, allowing younger users to be aware of how much time they spend on the app and requiring that they make active decisions to extend the recommended screen time. These weekly updates are available now, alongside prompts to encourage teens to use screen time tools.

The changes seem designed to make users more aware of their screen time

TikTok says it consulted current academic research and experts from the Digital Wellness Lab at Boston Children’s Hospital when deciding how long the time restriction should be.

“While there’s no collectively-endorsed position on how much screen time is ‘too much’, or even the impact of screen time more broadly, we recognize that teens typically require extra support as they start to explore the online world independently,” said Cormac Keenan, Head of Trust and Safety at TikTok, in a statement. 

The 60 minute time limit will also apply to children under the age of 13 using the “TikTok for Younger Users” limited app experience. In this instance, a parent or guardian will need to set or enter an existing passcode to enable 30 minutes of additional watch time on the account if the screen time limit is reached.

Four new features are also being added to Family Pairing, TikTok’s customizable parental controls that allow a parent or guardian to link their TikTok account to a younger user’s account. Custom limits can be applied, allowing restrictions to be adjusted based on what day of the week it is (or more widely extended over school holidays).

New features for Family Pairing provide a screen time dashboard for parents and the ability to mute TikTok notifications on their childs device.

Family Pairing will also grant access to TikTok’s screen time dashboard that summarizes how much time a child has spent on the app, how often it was opened, and a breakdown detailing how much time was spent during the day and night. A new “Mute Notifications” setting will soon allow parents to set a schedule to mute app notifications on their children’s accounts. Push notifications are already muted automatically from 9PM for users between 13 and 15 years old, while 16-17 year-olds have push notifications disabled from 10PM.

Finally, TikTok says it’s developing new content controls that will allow caregivers to filter videos with words or hashtags they don’t want their children to watch. The company is working with “parenting, youth, and civil society organizations” over the coming weeks to design the feature.

Outside of Family Pairing, TikTok said that some of these improvements will be made widely available, allowing any user to schedule mute notifications and set customized screen time limits for each day of the week. A sleep reminder is also now available that allows users to set a time to be reminded to close the app and go to bed.

TikTok spokesperson Mahsau Cullinane informed The Verge that the new default screen time limit for teens, customizable daily time limits, Mute Notifications feature, and all Family Pairing improvements will roll out over the coming weeks.

The 60 minute time limit will also apply to children under the age of 13 using the “TikTok for Younger Users” limited app experience. In this instance, a parent or guardian will need to set or enter an existing passcode to enable 30 minutes of additional watch time on the account if the screen time limit is reached.

Custom limits can be applied, allowing restrictions to be adjusted based on what day of the week it is (or more widely extended over school holidays).

LEX., Financial Times, 17 November 2021
Who’s afraid of the big, bad price rise? Not Americans. US inflation may have hit a 31-year high in October. But consumers are still eager to spend.
This should be good news for Walmart. The world’s biggest bricks-and-mortar retailer reported strong third-quarter sales and raised its full-year outlook. Supply-chain disruptions and fears of empty shelves are prompting many Americans to get a head start on their holiday shopping.
Do not be fooled by the topline growth. There are reasons that shares in Walmart have gone nowhere this year. The stock is down 3 per cent, compared with the 48 per cent gains at rivals Target and Home Depot.
To ensure that its shelves are stocked for the holidays, Walmart has taken drastic measures, including using air freight and chartering its own cargo ships. This has helped it to increase US inventory 11.5 per cent in the quarter.
That has come at a cost. Gross quarterly margins fell 42 basis points to 24.6 per cent. This compares with 34.1 per cent at Home Depot and the 30 per cent posted by Target.
Pressure will persist. Labour shortages mean low-wage Walmart will need to pay up for workers. Home Depot sells bulky items that cannot be readily ordered from Amazon. Target has strong in-house brands that help protect margins. But Walmart is more exposed to the inflationary squeeze.
Many of the products it carries can readily be bought elsewhere.
Walmart still trades at a premium to Target, which is on 21 times forward earnings. But the
valuation has fallen from 27 to 23 times over the past year.
To break out of rangebound trading, Walmart will have to find new sources of growth. Potential
catalysts include Walmart’s ad unit and its marketplace business where third-party vendors sell their wares. Walmart, once written off as a doomed physical retailer, has staged a remarkable recovery. The era of rising inflation means another reinvention is required.

Thus the likelihood that tourists will utilize these services is low. Figure 3 presents the results of the calculation of cumulative effective distance to all tourist sites studied, ordered by CED. For each tourist destination, the CED from all hotels and hostels was calculated. As can be seen in Figure 3, Jaffa gate (and Mamilla), the Garden Tomb and Mahane Yehuda market, are the most accessible destinations in Jerusalem, mainly due to their central location and proximity to the LRT line. While the new calculation does not ignore the presence of Kavey Mehadrin in the city, it reduces their visibility by increasing the cost level. In other words, such bus lines receive a lower visibility rate. The results of the new calculation are presented in Figure 4. The percentage of change (the black dots relating to the right hand scale) represent the implications of the lower visibility of the available bus service for tourist. The black dots show that several destinations were substantially (adversely) affected. Once the LRT and Egged services are calculated as being the most visible to tourists the CED of destinations such as the City of David, Jaffa Gate and Mamilla, Gethsemane and Commissioner Palace Promenade, rises by more than 30% (and hence their accessibility diminishes). These results demonstrate the problems tourists face when attempting to use public transportation in Jerusalem as the main mode of travel. Moreover, the difference between the two calculations of CED highlights the gap between how urban and transport planners perceive the level of service of the public transportation in Jerusalem and how tourists experience it.

The Bispectral Index (BIS) Module is a medical device designed to aid in the monitoring, recording, and alarming of multiple physiological parameters of adults, pediatrics, and neonates by utilizing EEG signals. The Bispectral Index (BIS) Module continuously processes a patient’s electroencephalographic (EEG) signal to calculate a single BIS value ranging from 100 (fully awake) to 0 (absence of electrical brain activity). The Bispectral Index (BIS) Module is designed to provide a measure of the hypnotic effects of anesthetic and sedative agents on the brain. In the operating room, it is used to monitor a patient’s risk of awareness and is intended to reduce hypnotic drug usage, achieve faster wake-up from anesthesia, and have faster qualification for discharge from the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU). In the intensive care unit, it is used to assess the patient’s level of sedation objectively and is intended to reduce sedative drug usage, decrease the number of ventilation days, and improve patient comfort. 

The Bispectral Index (BIS) Module is intended to be used with IntelliVue MP and MX models of patient monitors.

CHAPTER TWO
 Jeremy’s Story
 From Jeremy
I got into the business of healing back pain because I had serious back pain myself, as a young man, caused by a series of athletic injuries. I got into chiropractic and related whole-body disciplines because nothing else worked for me. I went on to develop my own, very different variations on familiar chiropractic practices over time. I do not “pop” backs or any of that, but I draw heavily on the basic elements of the discipline, as well as my reading of the scientific literature generally and my own considerable experience as a practitioner.
I grew up in a traditional medical household, and fully expected to go to medical school and then into practice. My grandfather was a medical doctor, my father is a medical doctor, my mom is a nurse, my aunt is a nurse, my uncle was a pharmaceutical salesman. I was as deeply immersed in traditional Western medicine as one could possibly be, and I had—and still have—tremendous respect for it. When I was little, I was used to having people come up to me and tell me how much my grandfather had done to save this or that child from some grim fate. He was one of those doctors that they don’t really make anymore. He performed surgeries, delivered babies, made house calls, and was a master diagnostician. And he was also a terrific guy whom I admired a lot. Later I heard the same things about my parents from their patients. 
So I grew up believing there wasn’t much that modern medicine could not fix, and I couldn’t wait to become a part of it. I emphasize all this because, eventually, I am going to sound a bit reserved about traditional Western medicine and back pain, and I don’t want you to be confused: I revere traditional medicine and understand it better than most. It’s just that it generally isn’t great at curing back pain. And back pain is what I had as a young man . . . a lot of it. And it has been my life ever since. 
My Personal Pain: Part One 
When I was a teenager, I thought I was going to be a professional skateboarder. If you are over fifty, do not snap the book closed at this point; skateboarding is a terrific sport. But it is a slightly dangerous sport and I took many, many falls, some of them pretty bad. I did not become a professional skateboarder; I might have been good enough, but long before that could happen I became a very young man with extremely serious back pain. When that happened, I went the traditional medical route. I went to regular doctors (good ones, as you’d expect) and was poked and prodded; I had ultrasounds and MRIs and blood tests and you-name-it. They talked about an extraordinary range of possible causes, including “slipped discs,” “ruptured discs,” “pinched nerves,” maybe cancer. Wow! But they could not fix my pain. I was somewhat medically astute, even as a kid, and I became increasingly convinced that a lot of these well-meaning, well-trained doctors didn’t really know an awful lot about my back pain. Sounds harsh, but it has turned out to be true of quite a few conventional doctors. 
In near desperation, I turned to less traditional medicine—to chiropractors. And darned if I didn’t find at least some symptomatic relief. That was huge, and it opened my head to the possibility of going in that direction. I should mention that those particular chiropractors weren’t perfect, either. They didn’t begin to teach me how to make fundamental changes. They didn’t talk about changing my own behaviors or suggest how to take control of my own health or do any of the things that are at the heart of my practice today. But they did show me that the pain could be affected with simple muscle and joint work, and I was deeply impressed by that. Chiropractic treatment has its place in back care and offers many benefits when done properly. Skilled chiropractors use manual (with their hands) therapy to restore normal joint movement and muscle function through chiropractic adjustments and other techniques such as stretching and joint mobilization. This therapy can be invaluable, especially in the short term. But even today many chiropractors do not teach their patients how to make the necessary behavioral changes to permanently relieve back pain. 
I decided to train in chiropractic, because I wanted to dig deeper into what I already recognized as the real causes—and perhaps the real treatment—of serious back pain: behavior and behavioral change. That drove my very medical family crazy, as you can imagine, but in retrospect it was exactly the right decision. 
My education was a long and complex process. I took guidance from a range of experts in the chiropractic and other fields. But I eventually developed my own analyses and my own approach to permanently ending back pain in my patients. Traditional medicine takes a basically deconstructivist approach: It generally takes complex problems apart, analyzes the pieces with exquisite care, then identifies and cures the particular problem. That deconstructivist approach works miraculously for many, many medical problems, but not for back pain. For back pain you want an integrationist approach. You want whole-body solutions.
My Personal Pain: Part Two 
I had a second round of back pain, long after I should have known better, and I want to tell you that embarrassing story for several reasons. First, because the pain was so dreadful, and I want you to know just how deeply I understand and empathize with significant pain. Second, I want to stress just how vulnerable all of us are to default behaviors that can raise holy hell with our backs, including people like me, who surely should have known better. And third, I want to show how quickly and effectively you can deal with even the gravest back pain, once you know what you’re doing. 
The time is seven years ago. I was working part of the time on a very promising medical start-up venture. For six months, I was absolutely obsessed with it. I worked regular ten- and twelve-hour days with few breaks for leisure or exercise. Most of the time, I was bent over my computer. I worked like an absolute lunatic and did not think twice about my back. Pathetic. 
One morning, after a particularly grueling stretch of days and nights, I woke up at six and started to sit up to go to the john. I was smacked by the most ferocious pain I’ve ever had in my life, even worse than anything from my skateboarding days. I was knocked flat on my back and could not budge. Even when I was lying absolutely still, the pain continued, unabated, at a fierce level. If I tried to move, it was much, much worse. I lived alone back then, and all I could do was lie there and wonder, in near panic: What in the world is going on? Just how bad is this? Am I going to die, for heaven’s sake? Not only was I in terrible pain; I was seriously scared. 
I remembered how “normal” back pain felt, a bad spasm or whatever. But this seemed to be way beyond that. So what was it? A ruptured disc would be the good news. At the other end of the spectrum, perhaps it was some weird cancer, somewhere in my spine. 
That was ridiculous, but truly severe pain leads to some wild and unpredictable thoughts. I was sweating and breathing hard and was on the edge of panic. And that went on for what seemed like forever. At last my long scientific training and experience took over. The first step was to ask myself the questions I ask all my patients: How did this happen? What “behavior” might have caused this? It’s interesting just how often the sufferer knows intuitively what he or she had done (at least the triggering event) and I was no different. It did not take long to conclude that it was probably those months of nonstop work, bent over a computer. Of course! For someone with my history, that was nuts. And step one was to stop doing what had caused the pain in the first place. (If I ever managed to sit or stand again.) The problem right now was to ease the pain and move. With more than a little agony, I rolled onto my side to see if I could stand. I couldn’t. The pain ratcheted up to new levels and slapped me flat on my back again. It felt as if someone were stabbing me in my kidneys and dragging the knife down into my buttocks. It literally took my breath away. 
Then it was back to basics: I did what I always do in those relatively rare cases when I’m there during a patient’s attack. I told myself to tense my abdominal muscles a little and slowly pick up my left foot. I am lying flat in bed and picking up one foot, just a little bit. That simple first step, which I have counseled so many times, was bearable. It almost always is. I set that foot down and picked up the right foot, continuing to tense my abdominal muscles. That also was doable. Good. Then on to the next phase: I walked carefully, very gently, in place—lying on my back and not lifting my feet very far—for perhaps five minutes. The pain slowly lessened. I stopped, and did it again several times. I was “walking off” the pain. And I was easing what almost certainly was a particularly bad muscle spasm, somewhere near my lumbar spine. 
Eventually, I felt ready to stand. I lightly tensed the muscles in my abdomen to support my spine and keep it still and rolled onto my side. As you will soon learn, this tensing of those muscles is called locking down or engaging your core. This time I could do it. I was careful to keep my lower back still and my abdomen braced throughout the movement. It was not pain-free, but I made it to my knees, then my feet. I was mighty careful to keep my lumbar spine still and my core engaged throughout, because I knew that, in the wake of an attack like this, the spasm and the pain were just waiting to come roaring back. Then I tried walking erect. And, yes, I could walk. I walked back and forth across the room carefully, keeping my core tight. I did that for quite a while and the spasm and pain calmed down. 
For the rest of that day, I was very careful about how I moved, and my back continued to get better. I knew from experience that those first steps would work because I had taught them to so many others. For the rest of the day, I took it easy and did no more than a little easy walking. By tomorrow, I assured myself, my back will slowly loosen up. It will take a week to return to normal, because the spasm was so strong. But in a week, I will be there. Then I will resume my regular exercise regimen, and stick to it religiously. I will not sit at the computer for more than thirty minutes at a time without taking a break and walking around. And so on and so forth. In fact, I did all that. In a week, I was moving and living normally. I did not let the intensity of my work interfere with my exercise regimen ever again. And the pain never returned. 
With my horror story behind us, I want to visit four other sufferers. But first, let Chris take you on a stroll down your own spine, and tell you about how your spine works and how it can go wrong.

start\_index = 1

# Define the limit
limit = 181

album\_info = []

while start\_index <= limit:
 # Create the URL with the current start index
 url = base\_url.format(start\_index)

 # Send a GET request to the URL with headers
 headers = {
 "user-agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10\_15\_7) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/110.0.0.0 Safari/537.36 Edg/110.0.1587.50"

 # Find all album info entries on the page

 # Loop through the album entries and extract the info
 for entry in album\_entries:
 album\_name = entry.find('a', attrs={"class":"ellipsis album\_name"}).text
 artist\_name = entry.find('span', attrs={"class":"checkEllipsis"}).text
 release\_date = entry.find('span', attrs={"class":"reg\_date"}).text
 album\_type = entry.find('span', attrs={"class":"vdo\_name"}).text

 # Add the album info to the list
 album\_info.append({

 'Release Date': release\_date,
 'Album Type': album\_type,
 'Listened To': ""
 })

# Create a file name with the current date
today = dt.now()

# Check if the JSON file already exists
if os.path.exists(file\_name + '.json'):
 # If the file exists, read the existing data and append the new data
 with open(file\_name + '.json', 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
 old\_data = json.load(f)

 # Add the new album info to the existing data
 old\_data.extend(x for x in album\_info if x not in old\_data)

 # Write the updated data to the JSON file
 with open(file\_name + '.json', 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
 json.dump(old\_data, f, ensure\_ascii=False, indent=2)

else:
 # If the file doesn't exist, create a new JSON file with the album info
 with open(file\_name + '.json', 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:

# Convert the JSON file to a pandas DataFrame and save as CSV

prompt:
John Hersey’s “Hiroshima” presents a moving and thought-provoking narrative that recounts the events surrounding the atomic bombing of the Japanese city of Hiroshima in August 1945. Hersey’s narrative is centered around six survivors of the blast, allowing for a powerful examination of the devastating aftermath of the bombing. By recounting the experiences of these individuals from their own unique perspectives, Hersey compellingly highlights the inhumane effects that resulted from the deployment of this destructive weapon. This review critically examines the book’s impact on the reader’s position on the dropping of the atomic bomb, the subsequent arms race, and whether focusing on the experiences of individuals who survived the bomb, rather than the leaders who developed and used it, makes a difference.
Right from the opening of the book, Hersey enthralls readers by plunging them headlong into the personal stories of six survivors, evoking a strong sense of empathy and compassion towards these ordinary individuals who had to endure the aftermath of the tragic event. Through vividly detailed accounts of their experiences and heartfelt feelings, readers are prompted to possibly rethink their stance on the use of nuclear arms as well as the resulting arms race (Hersey). These stories give a human face to the conflict and reveal the devastating consequences rather than just abstract concepts or statistics.
When evaluating the logic and rationale behind detonating the atomic bomb on Hiroshima, Hersey suggests that prioritizing survivors’ accounts rather than the leaders who instigated the bomb’s use can lead to different conclusions. Through their firsthand perspectives and an intimate portrayal of the tragedy’s aftermath, Hersey’s narrative invites readers to ponder the ethical implications of the bombing decision by challenging them to consider whether the decision was genuinely justified. By zeroing in on the six individuals, Hersey creates a connection between the reader and the people in Hiroshima, encouraging readers to see more than just a strategic military move, but a decision that affected the lives of countless innocent people.
By approaching the bombing of Hiroshima from the standpoint of survivors and their stories, “Hiroshima” provides an alternate and valuable perspective on the event and the resulting arms race. While it is crucial for historians to give attention to political leaders, military personnel, and strategic reasoning when examining the event, it is equally crucial not to overlook the experiences of the individuals who were deeply and directly affected, for it is their experiences that offer a significantly different and overlooked angle of the tragedy. Additionally, the stories of these six individuals may lead readers to question the necessity of the arms race and to ponder the potential ramifications of continued nuclear warfare.
In conclusion, “Hiroshima” provides an essential perspective on the consequences of the dropping of the atomic bomb and the subsequent arms race. By focusing on the experiences of the survivors rather than the leaders who deployed the bomb, Hersey encourages the reader to reconsider their stance on nuclear weapons and the arms race’s necessity. In an era in which the threat of nuclear weapons remains ever-present, books that examine the past with sensitivity and empathy, like “Hiroshima,” become more vital than ever. Encouraging readers to consider the human impact of war and the development of weapons of mass destruction could ultimately prove essential in avoiding the repetition of history and promoting a more peaceful world.

prompt:
(In the clubroom…)

Monika: “She should’ve been here by now…”

Yuri: “I’m starting to get worried…”

Sayori: (rushing in) “Who are you two waiting for?”

Monika: “Sayori! We’re waiting for Natsuki. She’s supposed to be here, but she’s running late.”

Yuri: “We hope she’s alright. It’s not like her to be so late.”

Sayori: “Oh, I see. Sorry, I guess I didn’t realize she was supposed to be here today. Is everything okay?”

Monika: “We’re not sure, but we’re getting worried. Natsuki usually notifies us if she’s going to be late.”

Yuri: “Yes, she’s never missed a club meeting without letting us know beforehand. I hope she’s not sick or something.”

Sayori: “Well, maybe something happened and she couldn’t inform us. Why don’t we try calling her?”

Monika: “That’s a good idea, Sayori. Let’s give it a try.”

(They all take out their phones and dial Natsuki’s number. It goes straight to voicemail.)

Yuri: “It seems like her phone is off.”

Sayori: “What could have happened? Should we go check on her?”

Monika: “I think that might be the best course of action. We can’t just sit here worrying. Let’s go to Natsuki’s house and see if everything is okay.”

(The three of them quickly gather their things and head out of the clubroom, heading towards Natsuki’s house. After arriving there, they find Natsuki in her room - she was heavily pregnant, and lying down on the bed in pain. Her breathing labored, and she was sweating profusely.)

Monika: “Natsuki! What happened? Why didn’t you let us know?”

Natsuki (weakly): “I… I didn’t expect it to happen so soon… I didn’t want to bother anyone…”

Yuri: “Don’t be silly, Natsuki! We’re here for you. Why didn’t you call an ambulance or something?”

Natsuki: “I was too scared… I didn’t want to be alone…”

Sayori: “Oh, Natsuki… You shouldn’t have gone through this alone. We’re here now, and we’re going to get you the help you need.”

Monika: “You’re right, Sayori. Natsuki, is there anything we can do to make you more comfortable?”

Natsuki: “I… I don’t know… My water broke and the contractions are getting stronger… I think I might need to push!”

Yuri: “We need to get you to the hospital right away, Natsuki. It’s not safe for you to deliver the baby at home.”

Natsuki: “Yuri, my contractions are too close together! I won’t make it to a hospital in time!”

Monika: “Okay, Natsuki, don’t panic. We’ll handle this. Yuri, Sayori, let’s make sure Natsuki’s baby is born safely.”

Yuri: “Alright”

Sayori: “We can do this!”

Natsuki: “P-P-Please! I-I-I don’t want to lose Sakura before she’s even born!”

Monika: “Natsuki, we won’t let anything happen to Sakura. We’re going to do everything we can to make sure she’s born safely.”

Yuri: “We’ll stay by your side and support you through this, Natsuki. Remember to breathe and stay as calm as you can.”

Sayori: “And don’t worry, Natsuki. We have faith in you, and we’ll be here every step of the way. Let’s focus on bringing Sakura into this world.”

(Together, Monika, Yuri, and Sayori assist Natsuki through the delivery process. They keep her as comfortable as possible, providing encouragement and reassurance.)

Monika: “Natsuki, you’re doing great! Just a little more, and we’ll get to meet Sakura.”

Yuri: “Breathe, Natsuki. You’re almost there. We believe in you.”

I meet the requirements for this role as ultimately I have a passion for child development and learning, both my own and children's. I am committed to my self-development as much as helping children with their own, most recently enrolling in a British Sign Language course. 

A good education should be for all, and I would love to be a part of helping children achieve their full potential through learning. I am enthusiastic, creative and energetic and as well as comfortable working in a busy and intense environment. I am experienced in working with children of all ages and abilities, and can adapt quickly to new individuals and experiences. I can think quickly on my feet whilst maintaining a responsible, calm and caring disposition, enforcing high expectations always. I am a firm believer in inclusion and equality, and would fully support children in engaging with each other and their work, whilst encouraging pupils to be as independent as possible. 

Through my previous employment as a School and College Engagement Ambassador, I have gained skills that would facilitate support for teachers, and support for pupils. I am also committed to supporting the school and believe in being sustainable wherever possible, adhering to the Green Statement. I am up to date on health and safety, confidentiality, safeguarding/child protection, and data protection laws and policies. I know basic first aid and I am confident in the event of an injury. Furthermore, I have good technical skills. 

Working at Red Gates School has given me experience putting theory into practice, and I am used to the school’s ethos and teaching style. I carry out the duties required for this job, such as classroom behaviour management, lunch/playground duty, and supporting learning through one-to-one and group teaching/support, and I am confident in my ability to perform them. I have a full understanding of classroom roles and responsibilities, and my place within them, and if I was successful in gaining this role, I would be fully committed to further development whereby I can gain new skills while building on previous ones. 

I pride myself on being a good, positive role model, and enjoy building relationships with all people. I would treat every child as an individual and learn as much as I can to support them in the best way possible for their individual needs, including IEPs and other plans they might have. I am comfortable building relationships with parents and I would give them the highest level of support to bridge any gap between home and school. Regarding teachers, I would aim to have a solid professional relationship with them, whereby I would keep them updated about pupils' problems, progress and achievements, and always be on hand when they need me. 

Overall, I would love to have this opportunity to inspire children and support them throughout their education at Red Gates.

summarize the following article.
It seems Oreos are as habit-forming as cocaine — for rats, anyhow.

At least that's what a new study has found. The study was run by science professor Joseph Schroeder and his students. It used rats to test foods with a lot of fat and sugar in them, to see if the foods might be making people addicted. In other words, would it be really hard for people to stop eating those foods?

The results? Rats seemed to like cookies as much as cocaine.

The study shows that foods with a lot of fat and sugar do the same thing to the brain that drugs do, Schroeder said. That may explain why some people can't stop eating them, even when "they know they are bad for them."

Rats Race To Oreos
The study was thought up by college student Jamie Honohan.

Honohan wondered why so many poor people are obese — that is, very overweight. She wanted to test the idea that high-fat, high-sugar foods are as addictive as drugs.

There was a reason Oreos were chosen, Schroeder said. The researchers wanted something that was tasty for humans as well as rats. That way the study would say something about "a problem facing humans."

Honohan said she also wanted to use something common in grocery stores. Plus, she noted, rats really like Oreos.

The researchers set up two little rooms for the rats. Then, they tried several different experiments.

In one experiment, rats were given Oreo cookies in one space and rice cakes in the other. It was clear that the rats preferred the Oreos, she said. They split the cookies apart and gobbled up the cream. Then, they went on to eat all the cookies. Not all the rice cakes got eaten.

After this, the food was removed. The rats were given the choice of where to spend time. They spent far more time in the room where the Oreos had been, than where the rice cakes had been.

Rats Get A Sugar High
The researchers did the same experiment with drugs. Rats were given a shot of cocaine in one room. And in the other room, they were injected with salt water. Then the shots were stopped. The rats were given the choice of which room to spend time in. They liked the room where the drugs had been better.

What did the researchers observe? The rats spent as many hours in the Oreos room as they did in the drug room.

Then the researchers looked at what was going on in the rats' brains. They wanted to figure out which the rats enjoyed more — eating cookies or being given drugs.

So they measured how active neurons were in the part of the rats' brain that feels pleasure. Neurons are nerve cells that carry "messages" in the brain. Rats and humans both have neurons. It turned out that the cookies activated many more neurons than the drugs did. In other words, the rats got more pleasure out of Oreos than cocaine.

This suggests that "high-fat, high-sugar foods are addictive," Schroeder said.

Hard To Quit Eating High-Sugar Foods
Honohan hopes people will learn something from the study. Maybe they will understand how hard it is to quit eating foods with a lot of fat and sugar.

Honohan said that in some ways, junk foods may be "more dangerous to society than drugs." This is because "you don't have to go (into) a dark alley to buy them. You go into any grocery store or bodega." And they are cheap. The cost makes them attractive to poor people.

As for Oreos, Honohan is done with them. She used to eat them before the study. "Now I can't even look at them," she said.

Have you ever wondered how literature reflects Indian society? O.V. Vijayan’s The Legends of Khasak is a great example of New Historicism, which examines literature in the context of the Indian identity and culture.
The novel tells the story of Ravi, a young man who journeys to Khasak, a mythical village, on the search for self-discovery and personal growth. Through his eyes, we witness the changing cultural landscape in India which is far removed from his own.
The novel is packed with symbolic metaphors and characters that reflect various aspects of Indian society such as religion, class structure and caste systems. We also see how Ravi's journey to Khasak reflects the struggles of identity crises in post-colonial India.
By analyzing O.V Vijayan’s The Legends of Khasak through New Historicism, we can gain a greater understanding of Indian identity and culture at this time period as well as their reflection in literature."

2.3. Previous work of Visual Assistive Technology
2.3.1. Head wear
2.3.1.1. Wearable Travel Aid for Environment Perception and Navigation of Visually Impaired People
 For this project, a consumer Red, Green, Blue, and Depth (RGB-D) camera was attached to a pair of eyeglasses, along with an inertial measurement unit (IMU) attached to a camera, a smartphone, and an earphone for commands/feedback. The system is operable in both indoor and outdoor settings. Due to their ample information, lightweight nature, and low cost compared to other sensors, such as ultrasonic and LiDAR sensors, computer vision technologies were integrated into this device's routing and detection capabilities. The smartphone does the process of detecting and routing, and the feedback is sent to the user's ear through an earphone plugged into the smartphone (Bai et al., 2019).
Limitation:
• Weak in detecting small-size obstacle
• Staircase detection is not implemented 
2.3.1.2. Let Blind People See: Real-Time Visual Recognition with Results Converted to 3D Audio
 Jiang et al. (2016) created a system that took video input from a portable camera. They streamed it to a server for real-time image recognition processing using the You Only Live Once (YOLO) model. The 3D location of the discovered object is derived by using the location and size of the object detection algorithm's bounding boxes. The Unity game engine will send it as 3D audio into their attached wireless earphones. The next sound output interval will be in a few seconds or when a different object is detected, whichever occurs first. The solution could conduct precise real-time objective detection with a live stream at a pace of 30 frames per second in 1080p resolution by utilising the YOLO algorithm and an enhanced wireless transmitter. Figure 4 shows the data flow pipeline of the paper’s system. The video footage is captured and sent to the YOLO algorithm for detecting object. The detected object is then send to the earbuds using the unity engine. Figure 5 shows the prototype of the device of this paper.
Limitation:
• Can only accurately detect and classify object within 2 to 5 meters away
• Surrounding ambient will be block when using earbuds
• Too much information will be sent to user when camera detect multiple objects
2.3.2. Smart Cane
2.3.2.1. Smart Electronic Stick for Visually Impaired using Android Application and Google’s Cloud Vision
 The e-stick module, integrated with a voice-controlled Android application, was designed by Bharatia et al. (2019) to replace the essential simple navigation stick that visually impaired individuals typically use. The e-stick is similar to a standard stick in that it is thin, lightweight, and easy to handle, but it has additional features. Using efficient natural language processing (NLP) features makes these functionalities affordable and possible. The e-stick uses ultrasonic sensors to find low-lying and knee-level obstacles and potholes when moving backwards. Using buzzers, active input on the presence of barriers will be delivered. For Global Positioning System (GPS) navigation to function, the user's phone will be Bluetooth-connected to the stick's circuit. In unavoidable circumstances, the live location of visually impaired individuals will be transmitted to the nearest help centre or their family for assistance. Face detection will be added so that users can tell who is trying to talk to them. With the cloud vision API, it is also possible to translate traffic lights and roadside signs so that blind people can find their way. Text recognition will also be available from photos, making it easy for people to read books, documents, newspapers, and other printed materials. A stick-tracking device has also been built in case the person loses his or her stick. These capabilities will be enabled through hardware (smart stick) and a software module (an Android application). Using Natural Language Processing technology, the user will tell these modules what to do by using voice commands. The e-stick will be charged as needed using a rechargeable circuit. Figure 6 shows how the technologies used in this paper interact.
Limitation:
• Coverage of obstacle detection is short as it is using sensor
• Only suitable for indoor
2.3.2.2. WeWalk
 WeWalk is a smart cane developed by a non-profit organisation called YGA (WeWALK Smart Cane – Smart Cane for the Visually Impaired, 2020). WeWalk looks like a traditional-looking cane, but the handle has a built-in touchpad. Users can navigate, save and discover places using the cane via the respected application. Particular layers are built into the mapping services for more accessible navigation. Users can choose to use the built-in speaker or Bluetooth for voice feedback. Users can also pair their phone with the intelligent cane via Bluetooth to control their phone. The above-ground The built-in ultrasound sensor detects an above-ground obstacle. The detected obstacle is projected back to the user in the form of vibration or audio, depending on the user’s preferences. Wewalk also has an application where users can view their transit options, such as nearby bus stops and the timetable, and then navigate them to the desired stop. The application also has a built-in voice assistant for more straightforward navigation through the application. If a user loses their phone or cane, they can play a sound on each of them to locate the position of the lost device. Figure 7 shows the WeWalk Smart Cane that is currently on the market.
Limitation:
• The device is very expansive, with the price of 500 USD
• Rain or snow might cause malfunction on the smart cane and the speaker
• The tip of the cane is loud when navigating rough surface sidewalk
2.3.2.3. Development of an Intelligent Cane for Visually Impaired Human Subjects
 Asati et al., (2019) designed an intelligent white cane that uses HR-SO4 ultrasonic sensors to identify obstacles within a range of 450 meters and determine the distance. The object above head level will also be detected, as the sensors' range is 450 meters. The warning signal is returned in beeping signals via a buzzer, advising the user to take prompt action. Object detection and classification are done utilizing the intelligent technique. The photos are recorded using the web camera for classification. They will be transformed into text and an audio signal for text-to-speech conversion. Figure 8 shows the prototype of this paper's intelligent cane.
Limitation:
• Cost of building the system is high
• Unable to identify pot holes
• Detection under rainy weather is not tested
 
2.3.3. Handheld
2.3.3.1. Android Application for Object Recognition Using Neural Networks for the Visually Impaired
 Dosi et al. (2018) have developed an Android application that aids the visually impaired with real-time object recognition using the phone's camera and provides feedback by speaking the recognised object. They opted for a deep learning strategy based on a convolutional neural network for improved recognition and faster response times. MobileNets is utilised because it is ideal for mobile and embedded vision applications. Figure 9 shows the results of the detected object using the object recognition application.
Limitation:
• Only works offline
• Unknown or untrained objects will be predicted using existing images in the database
• Have to retrain model for untrained object
2.3.3.2. Design and Implementation of an Embedded Real-Time System for Guiding Visually Impaired Individuals
 Duman et al. (2019) have developed and implemented a portable gadget that detects objects and measures their distance precisely to enable visually impaired individuals to see objects and people around them. The device uses YOLO, a convolutional neural network-based real-time identification method with a single device attached to a Raspberry Pi board. The estimated object distance will be projected in audio form to visually challenged users. The accuracy of this detected distance estimation is 98.8%. Initially, the footage is captured using a handheld Raspberry Pi camera. Afterwards, the object detection module executes YOLO for real-time object recognition, and bounding box size extraction for humans is needed. The size of the bounding box is provided to the distance estimation module to determine the distance of the detected individual. The labels of detected objects and the approximated distance of any individual caught are stored temporarily. An audio generation module translates text-based saved results into audio alerts that visually challenged users can listen to using headphones. Alerts are played at a predetermined time to reduce noise and ambiguity. Figure 10 shows the block diagram of the paper’s proposed system.
Limitation:
• Only detect humans
• No design for any wearable option 
2.3.3.3. Real-time object detection and face recognition system to assist the visually impaired
 Anish Aralikatti et al. (2020) developed an android application that used the phone camera for real-time object and face detection using OpenCV, the You only live once (YOLO) algorithm and FaceNet. Detection of objects and human will be presented in an audio format to the user. OpenCV is used for real-time computer vision tasks. Since it is implemented into an android phone, they chose Tiny YOLO as it is a lightweight YOLO framework perfect for embedded and mobile devices. FaceNet is used for face identification systems as it can extract high-quality features of the face. Figure 12 shows the sample outputs of using the android application on a mobile phone. Figure 11 shows the face recognition feature of the android application.
Limitation: Less accuracy than YOLO as Tiny YOLO model is smaller (Anish Aralikatti et al., 2020)

A crowd bustled at the Hammerlocke’s metro station in the Galar region. The streets were filled with excitement and anticipation as citizens eagerly awaited the arrival of their beloved Galar League champions, Gloria and Hop. Gloria and Hop had been childhood friends, their dreams entwined in those early years as they bonded over a shared love for Pokémon. As they grew older, their paths diverged slightly, with Gloria honing her skills in battling and Hop pursuing a career in Pokémon research. But their friendship remained strong, and they still journeyed together whenever they could, as part of their routine.

It was a bright and sunny morning, the sky a brilliant blue canvas painted with fluffy white clouds. The duo had just arrived at the metro station, feeling the warmth of the crowd’s adoration. Fans reached out for autographs and pictures, their faces filled with infectious joy. Gloria smiled brightly as she signed posters and posed for pictures, her Pokémon at her side, enjoying the attention.

Little did they know, all peace and beauty would be shattered in a matter of seconds.

A sudden piercing screech filled the air, causing everyone to turn their eyes skyward. A majestic Togekiss, usually a symbol of peace and joy, descended rapidly towards the ground. Panic rippled through the crowd as people scrambled to get out of its destructive path, a path they could not yet comprehend. The Togekiss let out a deafening wail, its cry carrying a haunting weight of despair and destruction.

Then, in an instant, chaos ensued.

The Togekiss exploded violently, its body becoming a lethal hailstorm of shattered debris. Time seemed to slow as the fragments rained down upon the unsuspecting crowd. Screams echoed through the air, blending with the sound of shattering bones and disintegrating life. People and Pokémon alike fell in droves, their bodies torn apart by the forceful explosion.

Gloria, in the midst of the chaos, had valiantly tried to shield her companions and Pokémon from the onslaught. But fate would not be kind to her that day. A shard of metal pierced through her shoulder, tearing through flesh and muscle, leaving her writhing in agony. Blood soaked through her clothes as she clutched the wound, feeling her strength drain away.

Dazed and overwhelmed, Gloria’s vision blurred and darkness crept at the corners of her sight. The pain receded, replaced by a numbing emptiness as she lost consciousness, slipping into the void of oblivion.

Meanwhile, Hop, her less severely injured companion, fought against the pandemonium that had consumed the metro station. Amidst the screams and chaos, he frantically searched for Gloria, his heart pounding in his chest. Fear and dread washed over him as he couldn’t find her amidst the sea of wounded and lifeless bodies.

Pushing through the crowd, Hop stumbled upon Gloria’s crumpled form, her lifeless eyes staring up at a world that had been forever altered. Her breathing was shallow, her pulse weak. He sank to his knees beside her, his hands trembling as he brushed a strand of blood-soaked hair from her face.

“Hang on, Gloria,” he pleaded, his voice filled with desperation. “We’re going to get you out of here. Just hold on.”

As Hop looked around, his eyes landed upon a group of paramedics rushing to aid the injured. He called out to them, his voice laced with urgency. They quickly responded, taking in the severity of Gloria’s wounds and rushing her onto a stretcher. Hop trailed behind them, his heart heavy with the weight of uncertainty.

Outside the chaos of the metro station, the city of Hammerlocke was in a state of shock. News of the tragedy spread like wildfire, capturing the attention of the entire region. The Human Supremacy Front, an extremist organization, wasted no time in claiming responsibility for the horrific incident. In a chilling statement, they declared it a punishment for the Galar regional government, a sickening display of power to further their twisted ideology.

The news devastated the region. Mourning and anger, like a tidal wave, rushed through the hearts of the citizens. They questioned how such hatred and violence could be unleashed upon their peaceful world. The streets that had once been filled with joy and excitement now lay desolate, haunted by the echoes of anguish and devastation.

As Gloria fought for her life in the cold, sterile walls of the hospital, the future of the Galar region seemed uncertain. The tragedy had left indelible scars, not only on the physical bodies of the injured but on the collective soul of the people.

Little did they know that the path to healing would be long and arduous, with darkness lurking around every corner. And in the depths of despair, a flicker of hope would ignite, kindled by the unbreakable spirit of those who refused to be silenced.

But first, they had to grapple with the overwhelming grief of losing their heroes, their champions, and confront the shadows that threatened to consume them all.

Before everyone leaves at the end of the working day, Mary gathers the team around in a circle. She seems to have a strange smile on her face.
"I want to thank you all for working really hard this week," she says, looking round at everyone. "I just wanted to let you all know how much I appreciate your efforts."
"I particularly want to thank Dan for taking part in a little experiment today," she says. Dan looks up, wondering what on earth she's on about.
"Thank you for all your hard work, Dan," she says, looking right at him. "You really deserve to go home and have a good *sleep!*" And she snaps her fingers.
Instantly Dan completely relaxes. His mind goes blank, his eyes close and his face goes slack as he suddenly spirals deep into a hypnotic trance, even more completely under than eariler. He slumps limply, mindlessly, in his seat as Mary explains to his colleagues.
"Dan was put under by a trained hypnotist earlier today and given the suggestion that he'd go back into trance whenever I snap my fingers and tell him to sleep."
Your collagues are amazed, amused, intrigued. Dan is oblivious to all of them, focusing only on Mary Brown's voice.

Dan opens his eyes and realizes with horror that somehow he was hypnotized in front of all his workmates. He is mortified. People are laughing at him. He just wants to get out of there, but before he can move, Mary snaps her fingers again and says simply, "Sleep!" and he cannot resist just dropping right back into a trance.
Dan slumps back into his seat, limp and blank like a rag doll. His mind is empty, and he is powerless to resist Mary's hypnotic command. 
"Ten times deeper, twenty times deeper, a hundred times deeper," says Mary, clearly enjoying the power she's having over Dan in front of everyone. "Now you'll do whatever I say, Dan. Open your eyes, but remain deeply hypnotized."

Ginchiyo: “Wait a minute, Nō. I’m sure this room was empty earlier. What’s going on?”

Nō: “Ah, you have a keen eye, Ginchiyo. This nursery was set up ahead of time. The REAL surprise will come in a few more months.”

prompt:
(It was finally time. I was in the clubroom, eagerly awaiting the arrival of my quintuplets. It hurt like hell, but my friends were there for me - Sayori had brought me some warm water to ease my labor pains, Yuri was bringing me some towels to wrap the babies around, and Monika helped me into the pool.)

Sayori: “You can do this, Natsuki! Just keep pushing!”

Monika: “The first baby’s coming through, Natsuki! Just a few more pushes!”

Yuri: “I didn’t expect for you to give birth now, Natsuki. I’ve still got a month to go to meet my little girl.”

(After several hours of labor, I finally gave birth to all five of my babies. I was exhausted, but overjoyed to meet my little ones.)

Natsuki: (breathing heavily) “They’re… they’re finally here…”

Sayori: “Oh my gosh, Natsuki, they’re so adorable!”

Monika: “Congratulations, Natsuki! You did amazing!”

Yuri: “They’re beautiful, Natsuki. You must be so proud.”

Natsuki: (teary-eyed) “Thank you, everyone. I… I can’t believe they’re finally here. My little miracles.”

(As the exhaustion took over, I leaned back in the pool, feeling a mix of relief and overwhelming happiness. The clubroom filled with a sense of awe and pure joy.)

Sayori: “What will you name them, Natsuki?”

Natsuki: (smiling) “I’ve been thinking about it. How about Rena, Kaito, Haruka, Sakura, and Emi?”

Monika: “I love those names! They’re perfect.”

Yuri: “They’re beautiful choices, Natsuki.”

(Each of us took turns holding my babies, smiling and cooing at their tiny new clubmates. The air was filled with love, friendship, and the promise of what the future held for my new babies.)

Natsuki: (softly) “Thank you all for being here with me. I couldn’t have done this without you.”

Sayori: “Of course, Natsuki. We’re always here for you.”

Monika: “Absolutely. We’re like a family, after all.”

Yuri: “You have so much love and support surrounding you, Natsuki. We’re here for you and your babies.”

(The room was filled with a warm and tender atmosphere as me, surrounded by my friends, embraced my new role as a mother. It was a moment I would cherish forever, and the beginning of a beautiful journey filled with love, laughter, and the bonds of friendship. But 6 months later, while I was taking care of my babies, I suddenly got a phone call from Yuri.)

Yuri: (surprisingly not in labor, despite being 14 months pregnant) “Hey, Natsuki. Don’t you think it’s surprising that I’m already 14 months pregnant but not in labor?”

Natsuki: (confused) “Wait, what?! 14 months pregnant? That doesn’t make any sense, Yuri. Is everything okay?”

Yuri: “I know it sounds strange, but it’s true. I haven’t experienced any signs of labor, and the doctors are baffled. They can’t explain it either.”

Natsuki: (concerned) “That’s really concerning, Yuri. You should go see a specialist or something. This isn’t normal.”

Yuri: “I’ve been to multiple specialists, Natsuki, and they’re just as puzzled as everyone else. They’ve never seen anything like it. But don’t worry, I’m taking all the necessary precautions and getting regular check-ups. My baby seems healthy.”

Natsuki: (worried) “I’m glad to hear that, Yuri. But it still doesn’t make sense. Is this some sort of medical anomaly?”

Yuri: “It seems that way. The doctors suspect there might be some sort of time dilation or abnormal growth rate happening with my baby. It’s incredibly rare, but apparently not unheard of.”

Natsuki: (thoughtful) “Well, I hope they figure it out soon, Yuri. It must be quite a burden on you. If you need anything, you know I’m here for you.”

Yuri: (grateful) “Thank you, Natsuki. I appreciate your support. And congratulations again on your quintuplets. They must be growing so fast.”

Natsuki: (smiling) “They really are. Time flies when you’re a parent. But let’s not forget about you and your mysterious pregnancy. We’ll figure this out, Yuri. I won’t let you go through this alone.”

Yuri: (softly) “Thank you, Natsuki. Your friendship means the world to me.”

(With their unusual circumstances, me and Yuri continued to support each other throughout their unique journeys. Although we faced unexpected challenges, our bond remained unbreakable as we navigated the joys and uncertainties of motherhood together - and I eagerly awaited the day Yuri went into labor. But 2 months later, when Yuri was 16 months pregnant, her labor still had yet to start.)

Natsuki: (concerned) “Yuri, it’s been 16 months and you’re still not in labor? This is really worrisome. Have you been able to find any answers or solutions?”

Yuri: (frustrated) “I’ve seen countless doctors, specialists, and researchers, Natsuki, but nobody can seem to explain what’s happening. It’s like my body is defying all medical knowledge.”

Natsuki: (determined) “We can’t give up, Yuri. There must be someone who can help us figure this out. Have you considered seeking a second opinion or trying alternative approaches?”

Yuri: (sighs) “Yes, I’ve explored various avenues, including alternative medicine and consulting with renowned experts from around the world. But so far, there’s been no breakthrough.”

Natsuki: (thoughtful) “Maybe we should reach out to the scientific community or participate in research studies. Perhaps they can shed some light on this situation.”

Yuri: (nodding) “That’s a good idea, Natsuki. It’s crucial that we gather as much information as possible and share our case with those who specialize in rare and unique medical conditions.”

Natsuki: (supportive) “We’ll find a way, Yuri. We won’t let you go through this alone. Your resilience and strength throughout this journey have been truly inspirational.”

Yuri: (grateful) “Thank you, Natsuki. I feel lucky to have you as my friend. Your unwavering support means more to me than words can express.”

(Despite the ongoing mystery surrounding Yuri’s prolonged pregnancy, we remained determined and hopeful. Together, we dove into extensive research, contacted medical professionals, and explored all avenues to unravel the enigma. As time passed, our bond grew stronger, fueled by our shared determination to find answers.)

Natsuki: “Yuri, I think I found a research institute that specializes in unusual pregnancies and reproductive anomalies. They might be able to help us. Shall I schedule an appointment for you?”

Yuri: (excited) “Yes, please, Natsuki! That sounds like a promising lead. I appreciate your dedication to finding a solution. Don’t worry, we will get to the bottom of this.”

(With renewed hope, we embarked on a new chapter in Yuri’s journey. We sought the guidance and expertise of the research institute, eager to find answers and bring an end to Yuri’s prolonged pregnancy. The road ahead was uncertain, but our friendship and determination would be the guiding force throughout.)

tptacek 4 days ago | parent | next [–]

We're talking about a product that has existed since 2004. They did:
\* Their own data center, before Docker existed

\* The non-K8s Docker way of deploying in AWS

\* The GCP, and then AWS, ways of doing K8s Docker

\* Docker in their own data center.

For 20 years of deployment, that doesn't look crazy to me.

The actual components of each environment are pretty standard. They wrote Capistrano, which predates Chef. Filebeat is a tiny part of ELK, which is the de facto standard logging stack. They use a smart reverse proxy, like... everybody else. It's easy to anything sound complicated if you expand the stack to as many acronyms as you can.

Simply put, the exigence of a rhetorical situation is the urgency, problem, or issue that a college assignment asks a student to respond to.

When Lloyd Bitzer drew attention to the importance of context in his famous article “The Rhetorical Situation,” he pointed out that certain aspects of the situation invite “the assistance of discourse.”[1] One of his examples is air pollution: “The pollution of our air is also a rhetorical exigence because its positive modification—reduction of pollution—strongly invites the assistance of discourse producing public awareness, indignation, and action of the right kind.”[2] Within a given context, certain elements or phenomena will provoke a call to action from discourse.

Some college assignments ask a student to brainstorm, research, and clearly articulate their own exigence and then respond to it. Other assignment prompts will provide a student with a pre-defined exigence and ask them to respond to or solve the problem using the skills they’ve been practicing in the course.

When analyzing texts or creating their own, students should be able to specify the particular urgency their discourse is responding to. It’s precisely this urgency that the text aims to take up and respond to, at the right time and place, kairotically. In thesis-driven academic essays, the exigence is usually clarified at the beginning, as part of the introduction.

When Lloyd Bitzer drew attention to the importance of context in his famous article “The Rhetorical Situation,” he pointed out that certain aspects of the situation invite “the assistance of discourse.”[1] One of his examples is air pollution: “The pollution of our air is also a rhetorical exigence because its positive modification—reduction of pollution—strongly invites the assistance of discourse producing public awareness, indignation, and action of the right kind.”[2] Within a given context, certain elements or phenomena will provoke a call to action from discourse.

Some college assignments ask a student to brainstorm, research, and clearly articulate their own exigence and then respond to it. Other assignment prompts will provide a student with a pre-defined exigence and ask them to respond to or solve the problem using the skills they’ve been practicing in the course.

When analyzing texts or creating their own, students should be able to specify the particular urgency their discourse is responding to. It’s precisely this urgency that the text aims to take up and respond to, at the right time and place, kairotically. In thesis-driven academic essays, the exigence is usually clarified at the beginning, as part of the introduction.
